newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-C&W says has held alliance talks.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-C&W says has held alliance talks.

text.p: Britain's Cable & Wireless Plc said on Wednesday it had held talks with US-based NYNEX Corp and other telecoms firms about possible new alliances, but emphasised it felt no need to align itself with a partner.
"I would characterise them as good business discussions," chief executive Richard Brown told Reuters in an interview.
"Where other companies have brought us opportunities to look at, we are responding to those ideas."

Cable & Wireless' plan to merge its UK Mercury unit with three cable operators including NYNEX CableComms Group has fuelled market speculation that C&W might seek to expand its alliance with NYNEX beyond the new cable company, called Cable & Wireless Communications.
"We would not limit what we may choose to do to just Cable and Wireless Communications," Brown said.
"We are talking beyond that, but I don't want to mislead you and have you believe they are the only company of any major scale we're talking to, because it's not."

"(This is) not to imply that there's some lock-up here that's imminent," he added. "That's not true at all. I have said we are large enough to be successfully independent and small enough to be nimble."
"The good thing is, we don't have to do anything. We are well-positioned globally, our financial performance is sound, and the wind of growth is in our sails," Brown said.
He declined to identify the other companies with which Cable & Wireless had talked.
"But I would say probably the only one we haven't seriously talked to is MCI with BT. We've left the door wide open for anybody interested to come and talk with us," he said.

Brown added that Cable & Wireless was well positioned to compete with the new company formed by the planned $20 billion merger of British Telecommunications Plc and U.S.-based MCI Communications Corp.
Cable & Wireless, whose own merger talks with BT broke down in May, currently competes with MCI in the U.S. through its CWI operations.
"CWI is now essentially a billion dollar business growing at 35 percent a year. And we don't believe the merger will slow that growth at all," Brown said.
"In the UK, we have fortified Mercury to form Cable & Wireless Communications and we think we've never been better positioned to take advantage of this market," he added.
Brown declined to speculate on the company's plans for its majority stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd ahead of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule next year.
"We would look at any formula that made good sense to shareholders," he said.
Cable & Wireless' pretax profits before exceptional items rose nine percent to 673 million stg for the first half ended September 30 compared with the year-ago period.
Analysts had expected the firm to post underlying profits of 650 to 668 million stg.
"These results are very good. They're not out of line with what we want to achieve as a world-class company," Brown said.
C&W's shares slipped 1.5p to 481.5 at 1005 GMT, after rising to 490 earlier.
-- Jeff Daeschner, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
